source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Vantage VA2 in Sterling publishes 96 MW of IT capacity. Among the 19 Virginia facilities on this site that have published a megawatt figure, VA2 ranks third, and its 96 MW represents roughly 7 percent of the 1,326 MW total published across those 19 sites. Virginia has 326 mapped facilities in total, meaning the overwhelming majority publish no capacity figure at all, so the true state total is larger by an unknown amount.

Ninety-six megawatts of IT load is a substantial block of power for AI workloads. Assuming 40 kW per rack, a common density for current AI training deployments, 96 MW supports roughly 2,400 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a figure more typical of general enterprise compute, the same power fills roughly 9,600 racks. Those are assumptions about density, not operator claims, and the published spec does not state rack count or supported density.

The operator page does not publish certifications, tenant names, pricing, or connectivity details for this facility. What the published number does establish is that VA2 sits in the highest tier of disclosed capacity in a state that is the densest concentration of data center infrastructure in the United States by the site's own mapped count, and a 96 MW campus in that market is large enough to matter as a building block for hyperscale or large-model AI workloads, provided power delivery and network interconnection meet the required specifications, neither of which is confirmed by the data available here.
